data.name: Rukmini
data.gender_notes: Rukmini is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit rukma, 'gold, radiance' — Rukmiṇī. Its root is Sanskrit rukma (रुक्म). Rukmini, wife of Krishna. Rukmini is a Sanskrit name meaning “Radiant; gold-adorned”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rukmini expresses “Radiant; gold-adorned”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit rukma, 'gold, radiance' — Rukmiṇī.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rukmini total 41, reducing to 5. Number 5 is associated with freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

vedic_reference.note: Rukmini is a prominent character in Hindu mythology, particularly in the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Purana. She is the chief queen of Krishna, who was abducted by Krishna when he was a young prince. Rukmini is considered to be an avatar of the goddess Lakshmi and is revered as a goddess in her own right.
